title: Zoom webhook secret token: two pages disagree on whether the token or only a hash is sent
summary: A webhook event notification, which one Zoom page says carries the secret token and another says carries only a hash of the body in the x-zm-signature header.
rationale: Claim secret-token-sent-wording records that two pages say Zoom sends the secret token in each event notification and name no header; claim secret-token-hash-wording records that the webhooks page says Zoom sends a hash in x-zm-signature and shows v0={HASHED_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TOKEN} in every header example. The wording conflict is an unresolved claim (carrier-wording-conflict) and neither page is preferred, so no carrier of the secret token value itself is documented (open question secret-token-carrier-unresolved). The derived outputs (signature, challenge, encrypted token) already have their own must-not-flag Case; this record covers the secret input's carrier. The era of the deprecated Verification Token is not pinned (verification-token-era) and no grammar is stated (value-grammar-unstated). Contract claims cited: webhook-secret-token/secret-token-sent-wording, webhook-secret-token/secret-token-hash-wording, webhook-secret-token/carrier-wording-conflict.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted for the secret token's carrier. Settled by: a Zoom statement reconciling the two pages, or a dated archived snapshot showing the wording changed.

sources.supports: **Secret Token** - Zoom sends the secret token in each event notification.
